/* ============================================================
   GOLD LAYER — DIMENSION TABLES
   Olist E-Commerce Analytics Project

   Purpose: builds the Gold-layer star schema dimensions from
   the cleaned Silver-layer Delta tables, using Synapse serverless
   SQL's CETAS (CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE AS SELECT) — the only way
   to persist query results in a serverless pool, since it has
   no native storage of its own and no INSERT/UPDATE support.

   Each dimension gets a surrogate key (a simple, stable integer)
   generated via ROW_NUMBER(), rather than relying on the natural
   business keys (customer_id, product_id, etc.) directly — this
   is standard Kimball-style dimensional modeling practice and
   keeps the fact table's foreign keys small and consistent.
   ============================================================ */

USE db_olist_gold;

/* ------------------------------------------------------------
   One-time setup (run once per environment, then leave commented
   out — re-running CREATE on an object that already exists errors)
   ------------------------------------------------------------
   - EXTERNAL DATA SOURCE: named shortcuts pointing at the Silver
     and Gold containers in ADLS Gen2, so later statements can
     reference 'silver_lake' / 'gold_lake' instead of full URLs.
   - EXTERNAL FILE FORMAT: tells CETAS to write its output as
     Parquet (CETAS always writes Parquet, regardless of what
     format the source data was in).

CREATE EXTERNAL DATA SOURCE silver_lake
WITH (LOCATION = 'abfss://silver@stolistdevweu.dfs.core.windows.net/');

CREATE EXTERNAL DATA SOURCE gold_lake
WITH (LOCATION = 'abfss://gold@stolistdevweu.dfs.core.windows.net/');

CREATE EXTERNAL FILE FORMAT parquet_ff
WITH (FORMAT_TYPE = PARQUET);
*/

/* ------------------------------------------------------------
   Drop existing tables before rebuilding, so this script can be
   re-run safely (e.g. by the automated pipeline) without manual
   cleanup. Synapse serverless SQL's DROP EXTERNAL TABLE does NOT
   support "IF EXISTS" directly, so we check sys.external_tables
   first and only drop when the table is actually there.

   Note: dropping the table only removes SQL's metadata pointer —
   it does NOT delete the underlying Parquet files in storage.
   The pipeline's cleanup step handles clearing those separately
   before this script runs, so CETAS doesn't hit a "location
   already exists" error below.
   ------------------------------------------------------------ */
IF EXISTS (SELECT * FROM sys.external_tables WHERE name = 'dim_customer')
    EXEC('DROP EXTERNAL TABLE dim_customer');
IF EXISTS (SELECT * FROM sys.external_tables WHERE name = 'dim_seller')
    EXEC('DROP EXTERNAL TABLE dim_seller');
IF EXISTS (SELECT * FROM sys.external_tables WHERE name = 'dim_product')
    EXEC('DROP EXTERNAL TABLE dim_product');
IF EXISTS (SELECT * FROM sys.external_tables WHERE name = 'dim_date')
    EXEC('DROP EXTERNAL TABLE dim_date');


/* ------------------------------------------------------------
   dim_customer
   One row per unique customer. Reads directly from the cleaned
   Silver Delta table via OPENROWSET; DISTINCT guards against any
   duplicate rows slipping through, and ROW_NUMBER() generates a
   deterministic surrogate key ordered by the natural key
   (customer_id), avoiding the non-determinism risk that comes
   from ordering by a non-unique column.
   ------------------------------------------------------------ */
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE dim_customer
WITH (LOCATION = 'dim_customer/', DATA_SOURCE = gold_lake, FILE_FORMAT = parquet_ff)
AS
SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY customer_id) AS customer_key, *
FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT customer_id, customer_unique_id, customer_city, customer_state, customer_zip_code_prefix
    FROM OPENROWSET(BULK 'olist_customers_dataset', DATA_SOURCE = 'silver_lake', FORMAT = 'DELTA') AS c
) AS c;

/* ------------------------------------------------------------
   dim_seller
   One row per unique seller, same pattern as dim_customer above.
   ------------------------------------------------------------ */
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE dim_seller
WITH (LOCATION = 'dim_seller/', DATA_SOURCE = gold_lake, FILE_FORMAT = parquet_ff)
AS
SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY seller_id) AS seller_key, *
FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT seller_id, seller_city, seller_state, seller_zip_code_prefix
    FROM OPENROWSET(BULK 'olist_sellers_dataset', DATA_SOURCE = 'silver_lake', FORMAT = 'DELTA') AS s
) AS s;

/* ------------------------------------------------------------
   dim_product
   One row per unique product, enriched with the English
   translation of its category name (LEFT JOIN so a product keeps
   its row even if no translation match exists — its English
   category name would just come back NULL in that case).
   ------------------------------------------------------------ */
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE dim_product
WITH (LOCATION = 'dim_product/', DATA_SOURCE = gold_lake, FILE_FORMAT = parquet_ff)
AS
SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY product_id) AS product_key, *
FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT p.product_id, p.product_category_name, t.product_category_name_english,
           p.product_weight_g, p.product_length_cm, p.product_height_cm, p.product_width_cm
    FROM OPENROWSET(BULK 'olist_products_dataset', DATA_SOURCE = 'silver_lake', FORMAT = 'DELTA') AS p
    LEFT JOIN OPENROWSET(BULK 'product_category_name_translation', DATA_SOURCE = 'silver_lake', FORMAT = 'DELTA') AS t
        ON p.product_category_name = t.product_category_name
) AS p;

/* ------------------------------------------------------------
   dim_date
   Full calendar dimension (2016-01-01 to 2018-12-31), pre-built
   in the Spark notebook and staged in Silver as 'dim_date_seed'.
   Unlike the other dimensions, this one does NOT get a
   ROW_NUMBER() surrogate key — its DateKey column (an integer in
   YYYYMMDD format, e.g. 20180315) already serves as a stable,
   human-readable surrogate key, which is standard practice for
   date dimensions in dimensional modeling.
   ------------------------------------------------------------ */
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE dim_date
WITH (
    LOCATION = 'dim_date/',
    DATA_SOURCE = gold_lake,
    FILE_FORMAT = parquet_ff
)
AS
SELECT *
FROM OPENROWSET(
    BULK 'dim_date_seed/',
    DATA_SOURCE = 'silver_lake',
    FORMAT = 'DELTA'
) AS rows;
